notes.front: According to the Guide, what body of theory does Kanban draw on?
notes.back: Established flow theory. The Guide’s list includes systems thinking, lean principles and queuing theory, among others.
notes.explanation: The Guide says continually improving a Kanban system based on these theories is one way to try to optimize the delivery of value.
notes.example: Systems thinking looks at the whole system rather than its parts; lean principles (Toyota has worked this way for decades) include producing only what is needed, when it is needed; variation is how much items differ, for example in size; quality control reviews whether output meets quality requirements; queuing theory deals with batch size and queue size, as in a line at a supermarket checkout.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Kanban Theory”, p. 4; Wikipedia, “Systems thinking”, “Lean manufacturing” and “Quality control” (lead sections); The Kanban Pocket Guide (Vacanti, Singh and Johnson, 2022), ch. 2 and ch. 5, PDF pp. 32–33 and 55

notes.front: The Guide’s list of the flow theory Kanban draws on includes lean principles, queuing theory, variation and quality control. Which item is missing?
notes.explanation: The full list is systems thinking, lean principles, queuing theory, variation and quality control, “including but not limited to” these.

notes.front: Which two things does the Guide name in brackets after queuing theory?
notes.explanation: They are the only theory in the list the Guide qualifies this way.

notes.front: The Guide introduces its list of flow theories with “including but not limited to”, so the list is {{c1::not exhaustive}}.
notes.explanation: Kanban may draw on other flow theory as well.

notes.front: According to the Guide, what is one way organizations can attempt to optimize the delivery of value?
notes.back: By continually improving a Kanban system based on these flow theories.
notes.explanation: The Guide presents it as one way, not the only way.

notes.front: What does the Guide say Kanban should do for other value-oriented approaches that share its theory?
notes.back: Augment them: “Kanban can and should be used to augment those delivery techniques.”
notes.explanation: Many existing value-oriented approaches share Kanban’s theoretical base, so Kanban adds to them rather than competing.

notes.front: A colleague says Kanban draws only on lean principles. Is that what the Guide says?
notes.back: No. The Guide names lean principles alongside systems thinking, queuing theory and others, and says the list is not exhaustive.
notes.explanation: The Guide’s list is “including but not limited to” five theories.

notes.front: A team already uses an established delivery approach and fears it must abandon it to adopt Kanban. What does the Guide say?
notes.back: It need not: Kanban can and should be used to augment delivery techniques that share its theory.
notes.explanation: The Guide sees shared theory as the reason Kanban fits alongside other value-oriented approaches.
